clusters.label: Real option definition and contrast with DCF/NPV
clusters.rationale: These candidates define real options and explain why they augment or address limitations of DCF/NPV by capturing flexibility and managerial adaptation. They are complementary foundational descriptions.

clusters.label: Learning and adaptive behavior as source of option value
clusters.rationale: These candidates emphasize that real option value arises from learning and adaptive behavior, enabling staged investments to outperform static NPV. They describe the same core intuition.

clusters.label: Payoff diagrams for identifying real options
clusters.rationale: These candidates focus on using payoff diagrams (call/put-like payoffs with kinks) to recognize embedded real options. They describe a visual, diagnostic method.

clusters.label: Definitional characteristics of a real option
clusters.rationale: This candidate lists the three necessary characteristics: defined underlying asset, contingent payoffs, and limited life. It is a compact checklist, distinct from the six determinants and tests.

clusters.label: Exclusivity as driver of significant option value
clusters.rationale: Both candidates underscore that without exclusivity, real options have no economic value. They illustrate through anecdotes and contrast with public market access.

clusters.label: Six determinants of real option value
clusters.rationale: These candidates enumerate the six factors (stock price, exercise price, uncertainty, time, dividends, interest rate) and explain their directional effects. They cover the same lever framework.

clusters.label: Replication and arbitrage principles in option pricing
clusters.rationale: This candidate explains the two principles (replication and arbitrage) that underpin option pricing models. It is a foundational theoretical concept.

clusters.label: Model choice: Black-Scholes vs. binomial for real options
clusters.rationale: This candidate compares Black-Scholes (European, constant variance) with binomial (flexible, data-intensive) for real option valuation. It addresses practical modeling trade-offs.

clusters.label: Three tests for applying real option valuation
clusters.rationale: This candidate outlines a three-step filter: identify embedded option, verify exclusivity, ensure tradeable underlying. It serves as a practical application checklist.

clusters.label: Proactive vs. reactive flexibility and lever influence
clusters.rationale: These candidates discuss how managers can actively change option value levers (proactive) versus waiting to exercise (reactive). They also cover the limited-player context enabling proactive moves.

clusters.label: Strategic lever selection via sensitivity analysis
clusters.rationale: This candidate describes prioritizing levers through sensitivity analysis, showing revenue/cost impact on option value. It is a practical decision-support step.
